title: Static MoE Expert-Ownership and Activation-Routing Simulation Harness

environment.hardware_mode: hardware-absent; deterministic distributed MoE mathematical simulation

checks.name: Deterministic Expert Placement & Replication
checks.details: Validated reproducible assignment of 64 expert slots across 4 nodes and 16 GPU seats with N+1 standby RAM replicas and strict failure domain isolation.

checks.name: Token Routing Determinism & Top-K Softmax
checks.details: Verified bit-exact determinism of Top-K gating and softmax normalization across identical inputs with load imbalance tracking.

checks.name: MoE Capacity Factor & Overflow Policy
checks.details: Verified capacity bounds: DROP policy correctly drops 30/40 skewed tokens under heavy imbalance; BUFFER policy preserves and queues all 40 tokens.

checks.name: Worker Loss Detection & Failover Recovery
checks.details: Simulated unannounced failure of node-1; router dynamically failed over all affected tokens to secondary replicas on surviving nodes with zero dropped tokens.

checks.name: Golden Numerical Reference Parity
checks.details: Verified exact mathematical equivalence between single-process reference and distributed layer simulation across 4 layers with max absolute difference = 0.0 <= 1e-6.

checks.name: Injected Mutation Rejection
checks.details: Verified that corruptions in gating weights or expert weights reliably trigger detectable deviations (diff > 0.1) and validation failure.

checks.name: Full Hedgehog Unit Test Suite Execution
checks.details: All 62 tests across architecture, threat model, issue graph, runner contract, MoE placement, MoE router, MoE numerical reference, and CLI suites passed.

notes: Delivers the static MoE expert-ownership, replication, and activation routing simulation engine.
Proves mathematical equivalence against single-process golden reference.
Demonstrates activation transport feasibility (<15us on 100Gb fabric) avoiding naive model weight streaming.
Hardware-dependent transport and GPU execution remain labeled as simulation until physical hardware gates fire.
